To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the acoustic length of an ear canal can be overestimated by up to 5% if the diameter of the connecting tube is less than 8 mm.

(1) the cross-sectional discontinuities at the interface between a rigid cavity and a narrow connecting tube cause errors in the "acoustical" estimation of cavity length and (2) a length correction was derived to compensate for this effect.
the cross-sectional discontinuities between the ear canal models and connecting tubes in the probe cause errors in the acoustic lengths.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the discontinuity at the ear canal probe on the acoustic length measurement of the ear canal.
the effect of the discontinuity at the cross-section of ear canal and probe on the estimation of ear canal length.
the effects of cross-sectional discontinuities on the acoustic length estimation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in order to obtain reliable ear canal length measurements with this kind of probes, the diameter of the ear canal models should be smaller than 8 mm, or the length correction should be applied.
the discontinuity between the ear canal and the tube is a source of error in the measurement of the ear canal length.
the probe tube diameter should not be larger than the ear canal diameter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cross-sectional discontinuities between ear canal and connecting tubes of a probe should be avoided.
, in the presence of a large diameter discontinuity, a correction factor should be applied to obtain a more accurate length measurement.
the acoustic lengths of ear canal models are underestimated by 0.5-0.6 mm when measured with the probe.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to obtain accurate estimates of the ear canal length, the probe tube should be as short as possible.
the cross-sectional discontinuities between ear canal models used for OAEs and the probe connecting tubes can lead to considerable errors in the estimation of ear canal length.
, in the presence of a cross-sectional discontinuity, the "acoustical" length estimation is not reliable and the correction is required to obtain the correct length.
